entities.name: Badis ben Habus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Badis ben Habus, the third Zirid king of the Taifa of Granada, presided over one of the most prosperous and politically complex periods of 11th-century Al-Andalus, reigning from 1038 until his death in 1073. His nearly four-decade rule saw the consolidation of Nasrid power in the southern Iberian Peninsula amidst the fragmentation of the Caliphate of Córdoba, establishing Granada as a prominent cultural and military hub. Badis navigated a volatile landscape of rival Taifa kingdoms and internal dynastic challenges, notably confronting the Abbadids of Seville and the Banu Dhi l-Nun of Toledo, while fostering a vibrant intellectual environment that attracted scholars and poets to his court.

Upon inheriting the throne from his father Habbus al-Muzaffar, Badis faced immediate threats to his fledgling kingdom. He successfully repelled an invasion by Zuhayr of Almería in 1038 and later orchestrated a decisive victory against Isma'il al-Zafir of Toledo in 1039 at the Battle of the Genil River, expanding Granadan influence. His reign was marked by the crucial role of Jewish viziers, particularly Samuel ibn Naghrillah (known as Samuel ha-Nagid) and his son Joseph ibn Naghrillah, who managed the kingdom's finances and foreign policy with exceptional skill. The construction of the Alhambra's first significant fortifications and the expansion of the Darro and Genil river defenses were also undertaken during his time, laying foundations for future splendor.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Badis ben Habus’s nearly four-decade reign stabilized and expanded the Taifa of Granada, making it a prominent regional power and a center of culture and learning in 11th-century Al-Andalus. His actions laid foundational elements for Granada's enduring legacy before its eventual fall to the Almoravids.
